answer: Running a farm therefore means funding each duplicate self through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent forfeits once and never again. Because the age is read from the zenith checkpoint rather than self-declared, the quartz audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 8 epochs old on the summit ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 17 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
